chunks: From him, from al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
The witr is three rak'ahs until the sun passes the meridian; then when it has passed, it is four rak'ahs.

key_terms.الشَّمْسِ: the sun, used here to mark the time boundary
key_terms.الْوِتْرُ: the witr prayer being discussed in this ruling
key_terms.ثَلَاثُ: three, indicating the number of rak'ahs before zawal
key_terms.زَوَالِ: the passing of the sun from the meridian, i.e. noon decline
key_terms.فَأَرْبَعُ: then four, indicating the changed number of rak'ahs after zawal

ai.seo_question: How is the qaḍāʾ of the witr prayer performed before and after zawal al-shams?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the qaḍāʾ of the witr prayer within the broader discussion of making up supererogatory prayers. It indicates that before zawal al-shams, the witr is made up as three rak'ahs, and after zawal al-shams, it is made up as four rak'ahs.
